title: eHealth-Integrated Psychosocial and Physical Interventions for Chronic Pain in Older Adults: Scoping Review
authors: Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso; Leo Benning; Deepak Singh; Annalisa De Lucia; Cinzia Perlini; Alessandro Chiarotto; Sara Pachera; Ilenia Pasini; Lidia Del Piccolo; Valeria Donisi
pain_condition_detail: chronic noncancer pain (CNCP) including osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, chronic musculoskeletal pain
bps_function_set: background framing; intervention rationale; organizing principle
bps_operationalization_summary: The paper uses BPS as an intervention rationale and organizing principle: it defines BPS as complex interaction of three domains, then operationalizes it by requiring included interventions to have both physical and psychosocial components. Outcomes are classified as pain, psychological, physical, and integrated (biopsychosocial). No mechanistic integration is proposed.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper describes associations between pain and psychological outcomes and between cognitive impairment and pain as bidirectional, but specifies no pathways or mediators.
quality_assessment_tools_1: qatsdd (quality assessment tool for studies with diverse designs)
conceptual_tensions_1: Paper defines BPS as interaction of three domains but only psychological domain is elaborated, social domain is minimal and biological is mentioned only as outcomes
conceptual_tensions_2: BPS is used as intervention rationale but no mechanism of how physical and psychosocial components interact is proposed
conceptual_tensions_3: Cognitive impairment and chronic pain are described as bidirectionally associated but no pathway or mediator is specified
additional_observations_1: The paper classifies outcomes into pain, psychological, physical, and integrated (biopsychosocial) categories, but the integrated category includes social participation and HRQoL without specifying how domains combine
additional_observations_2: The paper's operationalization of BPS is through inclusion criteria requiring both physical and psychosocial components, not through any integrative analysis
synthesis_note: This scoping review uses BPS as an intervention rationale and organizing principle for eHealth multimodal interventions in older adults. Psychological domain is elaborated with many constructs named but none defined. Social domain is minimal. No cross-domain mechanisms are proposed. BPS functions as a label for multidimensionality rather than integration.
coding_rationale: Typology is multifactorial: all three domains present but treated in parallel. Triadic integration is none because no three-domain relationship is articulated. Psychological domain is elaborated while biological is mentioned and social is minimal.

title: eHealth-Integrated Psychosocial and Physical Interventions for Chronic Pain in Older Adults: Scoping Review
authors: Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso; Leo Benning; Deepak Singh; Annalisa De Lucia; Cinzia Perlini; Alessandro Chiarotto; Sara Pachera; Ilenia Pasini; Lidia Del Piccolo; Valeria Donisi
pain_condition_detail: Chronic noncancer pain in older adults, including osteoarthritis/knee osteoarthritis, chronic low back pain, chronic musculoskeletal pain, and sciatica.
context_note: Included studies were from the United States, Germany, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and Thailand; many recruited participants from community-based settings.
bps_function_set: background framing; explanatory framework; intervention rationale; justification; organizing principle; policy or practice implication
bps_operationalization_summary: The review operationalizes BPS mainly by requiring eHealth interventions to combine physical and psychosocial components and by grouping outcomes into pain, psychological, physical, integrated biopsychosocial, and other categories. It synthesizes content and outcomes narratively but does not model cross-domain mechanisms.
integration_mechanism_summary: None proposed. The paper describes BPS as an interaction and lists physical, psychological, and social content or outcomes, but it does not specify mediators, moderators, or cross-domain processes.
quality_assessment_tools_1: quality assessment tool for studies with diverse designs (qatsdd)
bps_model_variants_2: biopsychosocial multimodal approach to CNCP management
conceptual_tensions_1: The paper invokes a BPS interaction but operationalizes it mainly as co-presence of physical and psychosocial components
conceptual_tensions_2: Social content appears as support or context rather than as a mechanism, despite social functioning and social participation being listed
conceptual_tensions_3: The review casts older adults as heterogeneous, but the evidence is concentrated in 65- to 75-year-olds
conceptual_tensions_4: Digital health is framed as improving access, while social support, family/caregiver help, and face-to-face care remain important
conceptual_tensions_5: Pain outcomes rely on self-report and numeric ratings, while the paper notes subjective interpretation and peak-end bias
additional_observations_1: The review excludes stand-alone physical and stand-alone psychosocial eHealth interventions, so the BPS frame is enforced at inclusion rather than analyzed as a mechanism
additional_observations_2: Outcomes are grouped as pain, psychological, physical, integrated biopsychosocial, and other, but pairwise links are mostly listed rather than modeled
additional_observations_3: eHealth delivery is heterogeneous: web-based programs, mHealth, teleconsulting/video consulting, VR, email, websites, smartphone apps, and wearable activity monitors
additional_observations_4: No spiritual or existential constructs are named
additional_observations_5: The article uses QATSDD but not AMSTAR, ROBIS, GRADE, or Cochrane risk of bias
additional_observations_6: Self-determination needs are named without naming self-determination theory
synthesis_note: This review operationalizes BPS mostly as an inclusion criterion for eHealth interventions combining physical and psychosocial components and as an outcome taxonomy. It names biological, psychological, and social content, but social factors are contextual and cross-domain links are mostly listed rather than modeled.
coding_rationale: BPS label frames scope and intervention content; biological, psychological, and social domains are present but parallel, with no specified mechanism, so multifactorial.

authors: Taiane de Azevedo Cardoso; Leo Benning; Deepak Singh; Annalisa De Lucia; Cinzia Perlini; Alessandro Chiarotto; Sara Pachera; Ilenia Pasini; Lidia Del Piccolo; Valeria Donisi
pain_condition_detail: chronic noncancer pain in older adults
context_note: International studies from US, Europe, Canada, Australia, Thailand
bps_operationalization_summary: The review uses BPS as an organizing principle to structure multimodal eHealth interventions combining physical and psychosocial components, but does not specify mechanisms of integration between domains.
quality_assessment_tools_1: quality assessment tool for studies with diverse designs
conceptual_tensions_1: Tension between BPS labeling and actual domain integration - domains are listed in parallel without specified mechanisms of interaction
conceptual_tensions_2: Limited representation of social factors - only 1 study considers family involvement despite its importance for older adults' eHealth adoption
conceptual_tensions_3: Biological factors treated as contextual rather than active constructs in the intervention design
additional_observations_1: The review maps eHealth multimodal interventions but does not critically examine the BPS model's operationalization
additional_observations_2: Interventions combine physical and psychosocial components through parallel module structure rather than integrated mechanisms
additional_observations_3: Quality assessment used QATSDD tool with studies rated medium to high quality
additional_observations_4: No study assessed frailty despite its relevance for older adults with chronic pain
synthesis_note: This scoping review maps eHealth multimodal interventions for chronic pain in older adults, using the biopsychosocial label as an organizing principle. The review finds that interventions combine physical and psychosocial components in parallel modules without specifying integration mechanisms between domains. Psychological constructs are well-developed (self-efficacy, catastrophizing, acceptance, kinesiophobia), while biological factors are mentioned only as contextual conditions and social factors minimally. The BPS label serves as background framing and organizational structure rather than an explanatory framework with mechanistic integration.
coding_rationale: BPS typology is 'multifactorial' because all three domains are present but treated in parallel without integration mechanisms. Psychological domain is 'elaborated' with 10 named constructs, biological is 'mentioned' with 3 contextual factors, social is 'mentioned' with 3 outcome measures. Integration is 'none' as no cross-domain pathways are specified.
